literal: we with eyes to see they laugh those without understanding, we experienced they not experiencing because
translation: Those without understanding laugh right before my eyes, because they have not suffered what I have suffered.
modern: நான் பட்ட துன்பத்தை அவர்கள் படாத காரணத்தால், அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் என் கண்ணெதிரிலேயே என்னைப் பார்த்துச் சிரிக்கிறார்கள்.
explanation: The speaker laments the mockery of the townspeople who do not understand the torment of love. The phrase 'யாம் கண்ணின் காண' means they laugh right in front of the speaker's eyes, showing a complete lack of empathy. They are called 'அறிவில்லார்' (those without understanding) because they judge without knowing the speaker's plight. The reason for their mockery is 'யாம் பட்ட தாம் படா ஆறு'—they have simply not experienced the suffering that the speaker is enduring. The poetic 'யாம்' (we) is used here by the speaker to refer to themselves.
